subject: VoiceChat-TTS: A Low-Latency Continuous Speech Synthesis Model for Interactive Agents

source_supported_claims: VoiceChat-TTS is presented as low-latency, continuous and streamable text-to-speech for interactive agents.
It is driven directly by LLM text-token streams.
It supports explicit interruption through control tokens.
It produces silence when no textual input is available.
It supports mid-utterance interruption without resetting the KV cache.

searched: Hugging Face for VoiceChat-TTS weights/model card
NVIDIA current speech/model surfaces for VoiceChat-TTS-specific release evidence
not_established_in_current_search: an official public VoiceChat-TTS implementation repository
a pinned local runtime revision, license and dependency set sufficient for reproducible execution
current_search_boundary.important_non_equivalence: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 VoiceChat / NemotronLabs VoiceChat is a separate full-duplex speech-to-speech model and must not be used as release evidence for the VoiceChat-TTS paper.

high_value_donor_mechanisms: continuous TTS driven from incremental LLM text tokens
silence as an explicit no-input behavior rather than synthetic filler
f2_relevance.why_it_matters: These mechanisms align unusually closely with Frankenstein's existing true-barge-in, cancellable-unheard-output and low-latency turn-taking requirements while preserving a modular TTS boundary.
f2_relevance.counterhypothesis: The paper's interaction semantics may be valuable while its released artifact status, German quality or hardware requirements make the model itself unsuitable for Frankenstein LOCAL-SOLO.
f2_relevance.cheap_falsifier: Locate an official VoiceChat-TTS code/model release that pins revision/license/dependencies and explicitly demonstrates German synthesis; absent that, do not dispatch a target-runtime benchmark.

promotion.reason: Source evidence supports the interaction architecture but does not currently establish a reproducible German local runtime candidate.
